primary_sources: Theodore Gentilz, Fall of the Alamo, 1844

stimulus.text: Theodore Gentilz painted this scene of the fall of the Alamo in 1844, eight years after the battle. The Alamo mission compound stands behind a wide open plain, and rows of soldiers stand in formation in the foreground.
stimulus.source_note: Painting viewed before writing: Theodore Gentilz, Fall of the Alamo, 1844, shared pool file u4/5s24-ch03-mcq-39.jpg, public domain. Gentilz painted the 1836 battle eight years after it happened; he was not an eyewitness.

source: original; stimulus image from the shared pool, Theodore Gentilz, Fall of the Alamo, 1844, public domain
stem: The painting shows the Alamo mission in San Antonio during the Texas rebellion. What does the scene most directly show?

options.text: American settlers signing a treaty with Mexico
options.misconception: The painting shows soldiers in formation before a mission, not a treaty signing.

options.text: Texan rebels building the Alamo mission in 1844
options.misconception: The mission was built long before, and the painting shows the 1836 battle, not construction.

options.text: Mexican troops attacking the Alamo during the Texas revolt
The United States Army annexing Texas in 1845
options.misconception: Annexation came in 1845, and the painting shows the 1836 battle, not annexation.

rationales.A: The painting shows soldiers in formation before a mission, not a treaty signing.
rationales.B: The mission was built long before, and the painting shows the 1836 battle, not construction.
rationales.C: Gentilz painted the fall of the Alamo, when Mexican troops stormed the mission held by Texan rebels in 1836.
rationales.D: Annexation came in 1845, and the painting shows the 1836 battle, not annexation.
rationales.general:
1. Read the image. Soldiers stand in formation before a walled mission compound.
2. Read the title. Gentilz called the painting the fall of the Alamo, the 1836 battle.
3. Put them together. The soldiers are the Mexican troops attacking the mission during the Texas revolt.
Background: Almost 200 Texan defenders died at the Alamo in March 1836.
Remember: a painting's title often tells you the event the image shows.
